summary: An iron-pile tower on a Biscayne reef, lit in 1878 to replace Cape Florida Light, automated in 1974 and now owned by Biscayne National Park.

The nomination gives the white flash as visible 15 miles in clear weather (unit not stated; the NPS page says 17 miles). Please check the current USCG Light List.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the story: deed date (1 May 1875 NRHP vs 6 Jan 1875 LighthouseFriends); superstructure contractor (Brown & Co. then Pusey, Jones per LF vs Pusey, Jones only per NRHP); second ship during construction (Carondelet per NRHP/LF vs Arratoon Apcar per NPS); automation 1974 (NRHP, LF) vs 1972 (NPS release); radio beacon 1943 (NRHP) vs radiobeacon and electrification 1931 (Bulletin); lens removal 1982 (NRHP implication) vs about 1984 (LF); Linda Lou outcome (Bulletin: sank; LF: told to cut loose for tow); characteristic change 1915 (Bulletin) vs c.1930 (LF). The 1934 Bulletin item gives only '8 December'; 1933 is from LighthouseFriends and the issue order (the next issue is March 1934). Yacht names in 1919/1927/1928 Bulletin items are badly OCR'd: 'Inwood' is LighthouseFriends's reading of 'Imvoocl'; the 1923 launch and 1927 yacht names are not given because unreadable. Bulletin 1926 hurricane: Fowey Rocks line is on PDF p. 49; the storm-centre sentence is probably p. 48, cited without page number via the volume URL. Lighthouse Board report volume 'annualreportlig01statgoog' is labelled 1893-94 by the corpus; the page header on the Fowey Rocks pages reads 1894, and the Columbian Exposition model is described there. Printed page numbers 240-241 for it are from the OCR page head (marked uncertain by corpus.py). The 1891-92 volume page is cited by scan page only. The NRHP listing date (26 January 2011) comes from HistoryPointer's reproduction of the NRIS record (NPGallery's own asset page carries scrambled metadata); verify against the NPS weekly list. Keepers: the roster is the USLHS list (125 lines). LighthouseFriends's list has extras (Thomas A. Moody 1923-25, J.W. Marshall 1921, Robinson 1960, Ken P. Roper 1965-67) and different 'Charner Smith 1944-45'; the Bulletin (1920 PDF p. 8) has James W. Marshall as assistant keeper in Dec 1919, earlier than LF's 1921. The Dec 1919 Bulletin text reads 'Weathe rford . l, eeper' (matched by reading, not by table position). The coastguardsman Riles killed 23 Dec 1942 (LF) may be the Edward E. Riles on the roster (1932-1942), but no source says so; not linked. Names of Coast Guard crew after 1960 are in the roster only (not in the prose). Rose Mallory (1950 reporter) is named only as LF names her; she may be living? likely not, but the anecdote is from one copyrighted source and paraphrased. The Frow log quote is as quoted by LighthouseFriends, not read from the log. The 'hurricane about three months after first lighting' is undated in the source. The tower height 130 ft (nomination) vs record 34 m (focal plane). Photos: none gathered.
